title: Linux Commands
label: Linux Commands
desc: Everyday command line moves for files, text, processes, packages and services on a Linux box.

sections.title: Files and Directories
sections.description: Navigate the tree, inspect what is there, and copy, move or remove entries.

snippets.code:
# Where am I, and what is here?
pwd
ls -lah /var/log
ls -lt ~/Downloads | head -n 5

# Build a directory tree, then copy it elsewhere
mkdir -p ~/proj/src/utils
cp -r ~/proj ~/backup/proj-2026-11

# Move or rename, and delete after a prompt
mv ~/Downloads/report.pdf ~/Documents/reports/q4-2026.pdf
rm -i ~/tmp/old-dump.sql

# Files changed in the last two days that are larger than 10 MB
find /home/felipe/Videos -type f -mtime -2 -size +10M

# Remove empty directories left behind in a build folder
find ./build -type d -empty -delete

# Run one command against every matching file
find ./config -name '*.json' -exec jq empty {} \;

sections.title: Viewing Files
sections.description: Read a file whole, page through it, or watch only its edges.

snippets.code:
# Follow a log while you work; Ctrl+C stops following, q leaves less
less +F /var/log/syslog

# The first and last lines, useful for configs and recent errors
head -n 20 ~/.bashrc
tail -n 50 /var/log/auth.log

# Identify the real format, then look at metadata
file ~/Downloads/archive.zip
stat /etc/hosts

# Count lines across a set of source files
wc -l src/*.rs

sections.title: Text Processing
sections.description: Filter, transform and summarise lines without leaving the shell.

snippets.code:
# Search recursively inside Rust sources
grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'unwrap()' src

# Keep only errors and warnings, then trim each line to its first fields
grep -E 'ERROR|WARN' /var/log/app.log | cut -d' ' -f1-3

# Replace every localhost in place
sed -i 's/localhost/127.0.0.1/g' config.ini

# Print regular accounts from the password database
awk -F: '$3 >= 1000 { print $1, $3 }' /etc/passwd

# The ten most frequent lines in a log
sort access.log | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 10

# Lowercase names and drop duplicates
tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' < names.txt | sort -u

sections.title: Permissions
sections.description: Decide who can read, write and execute each path on the filesystem.

snippets.code:
# Symbolic mode: add execute for the owner only
chmod u+x deploy.sh

# Numeric mode: owner read/write, group read, others nothing
chmod 640 ~/.ssh/config
chmod 700 ~/.ssh

# Recursive ownership change for a web application
chown -R felipe:www-data /srv/app/storage

# New files start as owner read/write, group read, others read
umask 022

# Share a single file with another account through an ACL
setfacl -m u:maria:rw /srv/shared/report.csv
getfacl /srv/shared/report.csv

sections.title: Processes
sections.description: Find what is running, see how much it costs, and stop it cleanly.

snippets.code:
# Largest memory users, then a program matched by its command line
ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 8
pgrep -af 'cargo run'

# Ask a process to exit, and force it only when it refuses
kill -TERM 4821
kill -KILL 4821

# Full state for one PID and the files it currently holds open
ps -o pid,ppid,stat,%cpu,%mem,cmd -p 4821
lsof -p 4821 | head -n 20

sections.title: System Information
sections.description: Ask the machine what it is: kernel, hardware, memory and load.

snippets.code:
uname -r       # kernel release
hostnamectl    # distribution, kernel and architecture
uptime         # load average and time since boot
free -h        # RAM and swap in human units

# CPU count and topology
nproc
lscpu | grep -E 'Model name|Socket|Thread|Core'

# Memory module details; reading SMBIOS needs root
sudo dmidecode -t memory | grep -E 'Size|Speed'

sections.title: Package Management
sections.description: Install, query and clean up software with apt or dnf.

snippets.code:
# Debian and Ubuntu
sudo apt update
apt search ripgrep
sudo apt install -y ripgrep
apt list --upgradable
sudo apt autoremove

# Fedora and RHEL family
sudo dnf install -y htop
dnf info neovim
sudo dnf upgrade --refresh

sections.title: Network
sections.description: Addresses, listening ports and quick reachability checks.

snippets.code:
ip -brief address   # interfaces and their addresses
ip route            # default gateway and routes
ss -tulpn           # TCP and UDP listeners with owning processes
ping -c 4 1.1.1.1   # four ICMP probes

# Resolve a name and check that a web endpoint answers
dig +short example.com A
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://example.com

sections.title: Disks and Filesystems
sections.description: See what is mounted, how full it is, and attach removable media.

snippets.code:
lsblk -f                    # block devices, filesystems and labels
df -hT                      # usage per mounted filesystem
du -sh ~/Projects/* | sort -h   # space used by each project

# Partition table of the first NVMe drive
sudo fdisk -l /dev/nvme0n1

# Mount a USB stick, confirm it, then unmount it
sudo mount /dev/sdb1 /mnt/usb
findmnt /mnt/usb
sudo umount /mnt/usb

sections.title: Archives
sections.description: Pack directories into tarballs or zip files and unpack them again.

snippets.code:
# Create, list and extract a gzip-compressed tarball
tar -czf backup-2026-11-04.tar.gz ~/Documents/reports
tar -tzf backup-2026-11-04.tar.gz | head -n 20
tar -xzf backup-2026-11-04.tar.gz -C /tmp/restore

# The zip equivalent, with a destination directory on extraction
zip -r site-2026-11-04.zip public/
unzip -l site-2026-11-04.zip
unzip site-2026-11-04.zip -d /srv/www

sections.title: Users and Groups
sections.description: Create accounts, change their groups and confirm their identity.

snippets.code:
id                  # uid, gid and every group of the current user
whoami
getent passwd felipe

# Add an account with a home directory and a bash shell
sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash maria
sudo passwd maria

# Grant docker access and confirm the new group list
sudo usermod -aG docker maria
groups maria

sections.title: Services
sections.description: Control unit lifecycles and read what a service unit actually runs.

snippets.code:
sudo systemctl status nginx
sudo systemctl restart nginx
systemctl is-enabled nginx
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running

# Enable at boot and start right away
sudo systemctl enable --now docker

# Inspect the unit file and a per-user service
systemctl cat sshd
systemctl --user status pipewire

sections.title: Logs
sections.description: Follow the journal and the plain log files under /var/log.

snippets.code:
# Restrict the journal by unit and by date
journalctl -u sshd --since '2026-11-01' --until '2026-11-04'

# Errors from the current boot, then a live stream
journalctl -p err -b
journalctl -f

# Plain-text logs still matter for many daemons
tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log
grep -i 'failed' /var/log/auth.log | tail -n 20
